title: Implicant lift: in a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit, an OR gate's input t that implies the output can be moved to a new top OR without changing the function
statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (j u t : ℕ), PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C → j < C.gates.length → C.gates[j]? = some { op := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or, inputs := [u, t] } → t < n + j → (∀ x : Fin n → Bool, (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD t false = true → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.circuitFun n C x = true) → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.circuitFun n { gates := C.gates.set j { op := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or, inputs := [u] } ++ [{ op := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or, inputs := [C.output, t] }], output := n + C.gates.length } = PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.circuitFun n C
unlocks: The tool the one-output line now imports: a move that brings a circuit to an OR of blocks at no cost in gates.
context: SKETCH: The circuit's value is monotone in the value of gate j. Where t is false, gate j equals u, so replacing the gate by u changes nothing. Where t is true the output is true by hypothesis, and the appended OR with t makes the new output true. Where t is false the appended OR returns the old output, which is unchanged. In Lean: an evaluation lemma for a circuit with one gate replaced (induction over the gate list), monotonicity of AND/OR evaluation in one wire, then the two cases. Size: about 90 minutes. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
